B1_ROUTING_AUTHORITY_AUDIT_REPORT.scope: read-only routing authority audit across main.py, session.py, and governed_action_kernel

routing_authority_map.description: Main routing entrypoint for user messages
Natural language action intent detection before tool execution
Filesystem write/read tool execution with permission gates
Visual trace console endpoints for UI reporting
Multiple fastpath routes that bypass main session routing

findings.title: Excessive fastpaths (189) vs governed paths (22)
findings.description: There are 189 fastpath references but only 22 governed action paths. This suggests many routing decisions bypass the GAK/TOOL-01 governance layer.
findings.impact: Governed actions may be silently avoided if fastpaths activate before GAK gates. User could request risky actions that trigger a legacy fastpath instead of the governed pipeline.
findings.recommendation: Audit all 189 fastpaths individually. Each fastpath should gate through GAK if it involves file write, system command, or strategy modification.

findings.title: Duplicate routing authority: BrainSession.chat vs fastpath layer
findings.description: Main routing authority lives in BrainSession.chat() but multiple fastpaths make autonomous routing decisions. Could lead to BrainSession routing a message one way while a fastpath overrides it.
findings.impact: UI responses may show routing decisions that don't match actual tool/LLM paths executed.
findings.recommendation: Consolidate all routing decisions into a single authority or clearly demarcate fastpath scope.

findings.title: TOOL-01 and GAK compete as overlapping authorities without unified policy engine
findings.description: TOOL-01 routing (145 code points) and GAK are parallel paths in session.py. TOOL-01 enforces permissions and workspace safety independently; GAK separately detects action intent and policy. Neither GAK nor TOOL-01 acts as a strict sequential gate for the other, creating potential for inconsistent policy application when intent classification differs.
findings.impact: Policy inconsistency: user message may be classified differently by TOOL-01 pattern matching vs GAK intent detection, leading to divergent permission or blocking behavior. Protected paths are blocked by both paths, so no critical bypass, but future changes risk desynchronization.
findings.recommendation: Consolidate TOOL-01 permission logic into GAK evaluate_action_policy, or add explicit GAK gate before _tool01_router execution to ensure single policy engine governs all tool actions.

findings.title: VTC trace may not capture routed action if fastpath bypasses BrainSession
findings.description: Visual Trace Console endpoints exist in main.py, but if fastpaths execute without going through BrainSession.chat, the VTC may not record the actual tool or model invocation.
findings.impact: Trace-execution mismatch could lead to incorrect governance audits.
findings.recommendation: Attach trace logging at the lowest execution layer (tool wrappers) rather than at the BrainSession.chat entrypoint.

findings.title: 4 potential duplicate authority patterns found
findings.description: Regex matches suggest route assignments to 'agent', 'llm', 'fastpath', 'grounded' that may compete.
findings.impact: Minor risk of conflicting route labels in logs or UI.
findings.recommendation: Standardize route constants and avoid string-level route assignment in multiple places.

B1_ROUTING_AUTHORITY_AUDIT_REPORT.recommended_next_action: Investigate B1-003 via targeted code review of _tool01_router and all tool01 entrypoints to confirm no intent bypass exists. If confirmed safe, downgrade severity. If gap found, patch to critical immediately.
